clue.text: Detective obliged to stow ring in hold at sea

indicators.note: to stow is to pack something away inside, so the first piece takes the rest within it

parts.note: obliged means bound, as in duty-bound

indicators.note: in places the ring-shaped letter inside the jumbled word
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of hold are jumbled

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A sleuth is bound to hide a stolen ring in a ship's hold during a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns HOLD into LODH; 'in' sets O inside to give LOODH, and 'to stow' puts that inside BOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogged tracker of people is nicknamed after the scent-following hound, so a sleuth is a slang synonym.

clue.text: Stable partition which may be jumped

explanation.surface: A horse clears the divider between stalls in its stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar dividing horses' stalls is one sense; the other is the bond money forfeited when an accused person skips court, idiomatically jumped.

clue.text: Oxbridge type involved in a race row?

definitions.text: Oxbridge type involved in a race row?

parts.words: Oxbridge type involved in a race row?
parts.note: reads like a university person caught up in a racial dispute, but describes a Boat Race crew member who rows

explanation.surface: A university person gets caught up in a quarrel about race.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford and Cambridge crews compete in the annual Boat Race, and each member of a crew pulls an oar.

clue.text: Unhappy at breaking a girl's hi fi cabinet.

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so a girl's gives DI'S

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so one word goes into the middle of the cabinet word

parts.note: a console is a cabinet housing a radio or record player

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at the smashing of a girl's stereo cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts AT inside CONSOLE, giving CONSOLATE after DI'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beyond comfort is a stronger synonym for being sad.

clue.text: Forgetfulness makes ex-pupil misplace 13's instrument

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: to misplace is to put in the wrong spot, so the instrument's letters are rearranged

parts.note: 13 across is VIOLINIST, whose instrument is the violin

explanation.surface: An old schoolboy loses another player's fiddle and blames his poor memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplace' turns VIOLIN into LIVION, placed after OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Total forgetting is the state of being lost from memory, a synonym.

clue.text: Race upset — first, Brown!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the joined pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: first is number one, abbreviated NO. I
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A racegoer exclaims that a favourite has been beaten, Brown coming home first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NOITAN round. 'first' as No. 1 (written NO I) is a common trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A people sharing descent, language and history may be called a race, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Self-satisfied, having rejected sweets

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the word for sweets is read backwards

parts.note: gums are chewy fruit sweets, as in wine gums

explanation.surface: A complacent person has turned down the sweets on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having rejected' turns GUMS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A complacent, pleased-with-oneself manner is a synonym.

clue.text: New Zealander losing ring accepts money for a drink

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece holds the other inside it
losing means a letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a Maori is a native New Zealander
a ring is round, like the letter O
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A man from New Zealand loses his ring but gets money for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops O from MAORI, leaving MARI; 'accepts' puts TIN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth cocktail is an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Use nothing, for example, thus scruffy as lodgings

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy and messed up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
EG abbreviates the Latin exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Advice to treat shabby rented rooms as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' rearranges USE, O, EG and THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hotel or boarding house offers rooms to stay in, an example of accommodation.

clue.text: Lacking purpose — sure to rile constituents

indicators.note: constituents are the component parts, so the letters of the phrase are rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: A politician without direction is sure to annoy the voters in the seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' points to the letters of SURE TO RILE as raw material; in the surface it means voters.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecisive and wavering means without firm resolve, a synonym.

clue.text: An actor leaves on it, perhaps :

explanation.surface: A performer exits the stage, perhaps climbing a set prop.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian and Edwardian London actor-manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated stage actor; a plant with a trunk carries foliage on its branches.

clue.text: What a cheek, flaunting such growth!

definitions.text: What a cheek, flaunting such growth!

parts.words: What a cheek, flaunting such growth!
parts.note: sounds like a complaint about impudence, but cheek is literal: hair grown on the side of the face

explanation.surface: Someone is outraged at a brazen display of ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: Long sideburns are hair growing down the face beside the ears, so a cheek displays them.

clue.text: Place for some flamboyant preacher

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the word sits inside flamboyant

explanation.surface: A showy preacher needs a stage to perform from.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters sit in the middle of fl-AMBO-yant, and the whole clue defines the pulpit.
explanation.definitionFit: An early Christian church raised reading desk or pulpit, from which scripture was read and sermons given.

clue.text: One playing at home embraced by another player?

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the word for at home sits within the player

parts.note: a violist plays the viola
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A footballer at home is hugged by a teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts IN inside VIOLIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler is a performer, so one playing music is a fair description.

clue.text: Mirror — a daily for the cleaner or polisher

parts.note: a looking glass is a mirror
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: The Mirror is a daily paper read by a cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid, and a daily is also a cleaner, so the surface is tidily misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpaper is an abrasive sheet used to smooth and buff surfaces.

clue.text: Yearns to play initially as a fielder

parts.note: to long is to yearn

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of play is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to join a cricket team in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the fielder placed behind the wicketkeeper to stop byes is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket position near the boundary behind the wicketkeeper names the player who occupies it.

clue.text: Backing the same company doctor

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for the same is read backwards

parts.note: idem is Latin for the same, used in references

explanation.surface: A firm's physician supports the policy as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns IDEM round to MEDI.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular informal word for a physician or medical student.

clue.text: It could have protected a muscle, they say

definitions.text: It could have protected a muscle, they say

parts.words: It could have protected a muscle, they say
parts.note: muscle is said like mussel, a mollusc whose hard casing shields it

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a body part was once guarded by armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A mollusc's hard outer casing, found on beaches, once guarded the creature living inside.

clue.text: Seat for a theologian in 24

indicators.note: in places the theologian inside the other word

parts.note: 24 across is the auction answer, a sale
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A chair for a divinity scholar is up for auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts DD inside SALE, the answer to 24.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits on a horse's leather seat, and a bicycle seat has the same name.

clue.text: Structural deficiency in the German fishing-boat

indicators.note: in puts the deficiency inside the German word

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
a rift is a crack or split in a structure

explanation.surface: A German vessel has a flaw in its build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RIFT inside DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that fishes with drift nets carries this name.

clue.text: Some colleges offer many such applied sciences

definitions.text: Some colleges offer many such applied sciences

parts.words: Some colleges offer many such applied sciences
parts.note: describes what technical colleges teach: practical industrial subjects

explanation.surface: Several colleges run a wide range of practical science courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical engineering and mechanical arts, the subjects taught at technical colleges, are known collectively by this plural.

clue.text: The Italian member Capone found under the counter

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the
a leg is a limb, or member of the body
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: An Italian gang member, Al Capone, is caught running bootleg goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Capone is the Prohibition-era Chicago mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold secretly or illicitly are said to be sold under the counter, an idiom for unlawful.

clue.text: The cad disposed to bring about a separation

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is inclined to break up a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges THE CAD; in the surface it means inclined.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or pull apart is to separate one thing from another.

clue.text: Such a sword is of no avail

explanation.surface: A blunt blade is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade without a sharp tip is literally blunt; figuratively the word means futile.

clue.text: Auction part of 29

indicators.note: part of means only a section, so the answer is found inside the other answer

parts.note: 29 across is the merchant who sells in bulk

explanation.surface: An auction is one aspect of a bulk trader's business.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside the 29 across answer: whole-SALE-r.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a sale by bidding, so the general word for selling covers it.

clue.text: The commotion it raised in the centre of Basrah!

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the central letters
the centre of picks the middle letters of Basrah
in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the word it reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: An uproar breaks out in the middle of the Iraqi city of Basra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns IT into TI; 'the centre of' takes SR from Basrah; 'in' puts TI between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or uproar, as in causing a stir, is a synonym for a commotion.

clue.text: Man or woman taking an hour to find the way

parts.note: Pat is a name for either a man or a woman
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Someone spends an hour trying to find the right route.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat can be short for Patrick or Patricia, hence man or woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A track or route is the way along which one walks, a synonym.

clue.text: Cause to hang about, say, for that thirteenth loaf?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so the phrase for causing delay is heard

parts.note: to make someone wait is to cause them to hang about

explanation.surface: A baker keeps customers waiting for an extra loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen: the extra loaf was added so the order would not fall short in weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown in to bring a quantity up to the required mass, like a baker's extra loaf.

clue.text: But was Ben Jonson of unusual density?

definitions.text: But was Ben Jonson of unusual density?

parts.words: But was Ben Jonson of unusual density?
parts.note: plays on the epitaph on the playwright's tomb, O ... Ben Jonson, and on the sense thin or low in density, as with air at altitude

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the playwright Ben Jonson was thick or slow.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson's tombstone in Westminster Abbey reads 'O rare Ben Jonson'; the word also means thin, as in rarefied air.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means uncommon and also thin or of low density, as with mountain air.

clue.text: As an able-bodied seaman, say, does he deliver the goods?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so the phrase is heard as a trade name

parts.note: a fit and healthy sailor is a whole sailor

explanation.surface: A fit sailor is asked whether he brings the cargo home.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole here means sound in body, so a healthy seaman is a whole sailor, said like the trade name.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant who sells goods in bulk to retailers supplies the stock, delivering the goods.
